title: Clinical practice guidelines for hypothyroidism in adults: cosponsored by the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists and the American Thyroid Association
authors: Garber JR, Cobin RH, Gharib H, Hennessey JV, Klein I, Mechanick JI, et al.
authorConflicts: One task force member reported speaker and program development honoraria from Abbott Nutrition; the other eight reported no relevant financial relationships with commercial interests. Of three acknowledged reviewers, one reported consultant fees from Genzyme and one speaker honoraria from Abbott Laboratories and consultant honoraria from Veracyte and Asuragen.
result: Recommendation 15: patients with TSH above 10 mIU/l are at increased risk of heart failure and cardiovascular mortality and should be considered for levothyroxine (Grade B, best evidence level 1; downgraded because the meta-analysis included no prospective interventional studies). Recommendation 16: treatment based on individual factors should be considered for TSH between the laboratory upper limit and 10 mIU/l, particularly with symptoms, positive TPO antibodies, or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure or their risk factors (Grade B). Recommendation 19.1: consider levothyroxine in women of childbearing age with TSH between 2.5 mIU/l and the upper limit of normal in the first trimester or when planning pregnancy. The text cites an NHANES III upper normal TSH of 4.12 mIU/l and a proposal to lower the upper limit to 2.5 mIU/l.
